title: UpdateApplication
description: The body of an administrative change to a registration, derived from identity_application::applications::UpdateApplication. Every field that changes something is OPTIONAL and every one of them ADDS. Nothing here removes a redirect URI, and that asymmetry is the design: a removed URI takes live clients down instantly and silently, so removal is a separate, deliberate operation that this contract does not describe.
x-serde-status: the type is IMPLEMENTED as a shape; UpdateApplicationCommand has no body and no route serves it

actor_id.description: The administrator making the change. A non-administrator is a Forbidden refusal.

display_name.description: A new display name, IF changing it. Absent means leave it alone — which is why this is Option<String> and not an empty string: an empty name is a refusal, and "unchanged" must be expressible.
display_name.x-serde-note: Option<String> with no skip_serializing_if, so the key is always present on the wire.

add_redirect_uris.description: Redirect URIs to ADD. Additive only, for the reason in the description above. An invalid URI in this list is a domain refusal and the whole update is refused — a partial application would leave a registration in a state nobody chose.

add_scopes.description: Scopes to ADD. Additive only, same reasoning.

status.description: A new status, IF changing it. retired is one-way: no later update can move a retired application back to active, so a caller that sets retired has made a one-way decision.
status.x-serde-note: Option<ApplicationStatus> with no skip_serializing_if, so the key is always present on the wire.

x-absent-fields.remove_redirect_uris: there is no such field, and its absence is the point. A removed URI takes live clients down instantly and silently; removal is a separate deliberate operation.
x-absent-fields.remove_scopes: same reasoning — narrowing a client's registration is a breaking change to a deployed integration
x-absent-fields.confidential: the confidential/public distinction is not editable. A client is registered as one or the other, and a secret-bearing client does not become public by a field write.

x-phase: Phase 5 — Applications, grants, and the self-service surface
